title: task edit fails on terminal-status records with misleading task_not_found
description: TaskService.editOn (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:774) looks up the target via findTask(snapshot.tasks, reference) - snapshot.tasks is documented as the active tasks/ location only. TaskService.moveTask (used by complete/archive/demote) instead uses this.taskRecords(snapshot), which is All task records, including retention locations. Once complete() relocates a record to .quest/completed/ (or archive() to archived/), every quest task edit operation against it - check-ac, add-note, final-summary, all of them, not just check-ac - throws RecordValidationError(task_not_found) via findTask, even though the record demonstrably exists on disk and quest task view <id> resolves it fine. Reproduced live on QCLI-218: ticking an AC while In Progress succeeded; completing the task then ticking or add-note on the same id both failed identically with task_not_found. This is why QCLI-217s six acceptance criteria could not be checked at close time despite having evidence for all of them, and is a likely root cause - not certainly the only one - behind the fleet-wide sweep opum-agent ran today that found 31 terminal records fleet-wide with unchecked acceptance criteria: any record where the author ticked boxes after calling task complete instead of before would hit exactly this. Scope is the lookup behavior and the error message, not whether terminal records should be editable at all - that is a separate design question this task does not take a position on.

acceptanceCriteria.text: editOn documented to state which task locations it searches, and whether that is deliberate or a bug

if unintentional: editOn (or the CLI layer above it) searches all locations edit is meant to support, not just the active tasks/ collection, OR the error is changed from task_not_found to a name that says the record exists but is not editable in its current location

the fix or the deliberate-scope decision is validated against the QCLI-218 repro (tick-before-complete succeeds, tick-after-complete on completed/archived should reflect the chosen behavior deliberately rather than by accident)
cross-referenced with QCLI-216 (phantom-AC checkbox integrity) as a related acceptance-criteria-integrity defect

implementationNotes: Independent Orbitfall confirmation from cli-test on 2026-09-04, installed Quest 0.3.2 (macOS ARM64). After CT-2 was completed, quest task view CT-2 --json succeeded and returned status Done, but quest task edit CT-2 --append-final-summary "..." --actor orbitfall-planner --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse --json returned exit 3 task_not_found. Recovery used demote, ordinary edit and complete, preserving the task data. This corroborates the existing lookup/diagnostic issue; it does not decide whether terminal edits should be allowed. Evidence: ../cli-test/project-artifacts/orbitfall/backlog-summary-addendum.json (error), backlog-retained-view.json (record exists), backlog-reopened-for-addendum.json, backlog-addendum.json and backlog-recompleted.json (recovery), plus commands.jsonl. No duplicate ticket created.

Live self-repro, 2026-09-05: attempted 'quest task edit QCLI-234 --add-note ...' on QCLI-234 (status Done, completed earlier the same session) to record a post-completion finding. Got exit 3, {"error_type":"not_found","message":"task_not_found"} - identical shape to QCLI-218's repro. 'quest task view QCLI-234 --json' resolves fine in the same breath, confirming the record exists and this is the documented findTask-vs-taskRecords location-scope bug, not a fluke. Workaround used: recorded the finding here instead, since QCLI-219 (this task) is still To Do and editable. The finding that couldn't be attached to QCLI-234 directly: PR #269 (dev->main promotion) failed source-gates on 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen' because bun.lock still pinned the six platform optionalDependencies at 0.3.2 after QCLI-234 bumped package.json to 0.3.3 without regenerating the lockfile - didn't surface on the version-bump PR because @opum-ai/quest-*@0.3.3 didn't exist on the registry yet to reconcile against; became visible once QCLI-234 published it. Fixed with a plain 'bun install --linker=isolated' plus frozen-lockfile and full check re-verification, both green.
